## Course Overview

## THIS IS A CSE 5000-LEVEL, PG-LEVEL COURSE

Introduction to state-of-the-art computer architectures, networks, and distributed systems for AI computing.

## Topics:

Lecture 01 --- Processor Evolution: from CPU to GPU

Lecture 02 --- Memory Evolution: Memory Hierarchy and SOTA Technie

Lecture 03 --- Network Evolution: From Kernel TCP/IP to RDMA and Scale-Out/Up

Lecture 04 --- LLM Era: Transformer and Its Application

Lecture 05 --- Constructing LLM Systems

## Tutorials

In addition to lectures, the tutorials develop practical skills for AI computing research and industry, including parallel programming, commonly used AI algorithms, and parallel algorithm design.

Putting Together and Project: Customizing Your Own Agents and Deployment

## This Course Does Not Do the Below

We do not teach a specific programming language. You are expected to learn or review the necessary programming skills independently.

We do not provide software-development support for commercial projects, internships, or part-time jobs. The course project is intended solely for learning and assessment. We will provide guidance and feedback, but you are responsible for designing and implementing your own system.

We cannot cover every topic in complete detail. We will explain the key concepts as clearly as possible, but some details will require independent study. If anything remains unclear after a lecture, we encourage you to:

• Search for relevant resources using Google, ChatGPT, or other appropriate tools.

Email us with specific questions, together with the resources you have consulted and your current understanding.

## Grading

Four Individual Coding Assignments: 40%

The assignments involve popular programs in AI computing, such as MPI, CUDA, algorithms, and parallelism.

One Course Project: 60%

Code repository accounts for 30%, we focus on the completeness and easy-to-use of your project.

Presentation accounts for 30%, we focus on the critical thinking behind your project. You are encouraged to apply the knowledge gained in this course to enhance its originality and technical depth.

## There are no exams in this course

You are therefore expected to spend more time and effort to the course project.

## Project Milestones

### I. Team Formation

Form a project team and confirm all members. Align on shared interests and working expectations.

### 2. Topic Selection and Proposal

Choose a focused task or scenario and submit a short proposal covering the motivation, planned system, and evaluation plan.

### 3. Project Development

Implement and evaluate the proposed system. Refine the scope and approach based on progress and feedback.

### 4. Final Presentation

Present the completed system and evaluation results, give a short demo, and submit the final code repository.

## Major High-Level Goals of This Course

■ Understand widely used and state-of-the-art techniques in AI infrastructure.

■ Design and build an end-to-end infrastructure stack for large language models.

■ Develop practical skills in multithreaded programming and AI algorithms that are valuable for research and industry careers.

## Takeaways

Becoming a good system architect is challenging.

■ Designing a new system requires considering many interconnected factors and developing strong intuition about design choices and trade-offs.

But, it is fun and can be very technically rewarding

## We hope that all of you will benefit greatly from this course!
